speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your history of diabetes, alcohol use, and recent weight loss, is there any specific area of numbness or pain in your right arm, such as between your fingers or around the elbow?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: The burning and dull aching pain you describe, combined with significant weight loss and a history of diabetes and alcohol use, raises concern for nerve compression or metabolic neuropathy. Do you notice any muscle wasting or thinning in the right arm compared to the left? REQUEST TEST: HbA1c, CBC, CMP, TSH. REQUEST IMAGES: Right_arm_MRI.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HbA1c: Not in data; CBC: WBC Within normal limits, Hemoglobin Within normal limits, Platelets Within normal limits; CMP: Not in data; TSH: Not in data; Right_arm_MRI: Not in data

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing Pancoast syndrome.

While the patient's previous provider suggested Multiple Sclerosis, his specific risk factors (heavy smoking, alcohol, steroid use) combined with unilateral arm weakness, burning pain, weight loss, and sensory loss are highly indicative of a lung apex tumor compressing the brachial plexus. The MRI and lab results I requested are critical for confirming this diagnosis and ruling out metabolic causes.
